question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode, and what ordering, approval, cancellation, and transcript semantics must it guarantee?
rationale: The current behavior gap is clear from source, but changing when tools start is a core runtime product/API decision rather than a narrow broken-contract repair.

options.title: Design opt-in core mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for a new execute-on-parse path with focused agent-loop, provider-stream, hook, cancellation, and ordering tests.

options.title: Keep current batch semantics
options.body: Close or defer the request if maintainers want the final assistant message to remain the only tool-dispatch boundary.

options.title: Prototype behind experiment
options.body: Allow an internal experiment first, but do not expose a user option until transcript and safety invariants are proven.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for a new execute-on-parse path with focused agent-loop, provider-stream, hook, cancellation, and ordering tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current main implementation and adjacent agent runtime parameter surface are most directly traceable to @vincentkoc in the available history.
